description: Canonicalization and content-hash fixtures in the record shape of contracts/v0/hashing.schema.json. Each entry holds the value inside the domain boundary, the expected canonical form, and the expected SHA-256 of the domain tag, one zero byte, and the canonical text. The two worked examples from contracts/v0/hashing.md appear unchanged. The Rust core is the authority; wrappers compare against these digests through the core.

hashes.note: Published worked example from contracts/v0/hashing.md. Reproduce it with sha256sum over the tag input, one zero byte, and the canonical text.
Object key order never changes the canonical form. The written order here lists proposed_message first.

value.prior_decision: Customer exports stay in the EU.

hashes.canonical: {"prior_decision":"Customer exports stay in the EU.","proposed_message":"Hello, EU export!"}

hashes.note: The same two members written in the opposite order give one canonical form and one hash.

hashes.note: A fraction serializes with its shortest round-trip form.
A zero fractional part serializes as a plain integer. Parsed 1.0 and parsed 1 agree.
Negative zero canonicalizes as 0. The sign of zero never reaches a hash.
A large magnitude uses exponent notation.
A small magnitude uses exponent notation.
An integer in range serializes without a fraction.
A precomposed accent is one code point.
A combining accent is its own code point. No normalization merges it, so this hash differs from the precomposed form.
An astral-plane character serializes literally.
The null character serializes as the escape \u0000, because canonical text cannot hold a raw control character.
A translation-domain hash covers one complete translated question value, a JSON string.
